summary: Feed s182_triple is degraded: 20.9% duplicates, VLAN 20 missing (50% untagged), and 31.43 Gbps microbursts overloading the 10 Gbps NDR port (314% capacity).

findings.root_cause: Traffic is duplicated before the NDR - likely overlapping SPAN/mirror sessions or multiple TAPs aggregated to one broker output without deduplication, causing the same packets to be delivered twice.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on 20.9% duplicate packets (1994/9522), inflates flow counts, confuses TCP state tracking and can cause false positives/missed detections.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication to remove duplicates before the NDR and restore accurate counts and detection fidelity.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN is stripping 802.1Q tags or not trunking VLAN 20 - 50% of packets arrive untagged and required VLAN 20 is never observed despite NDR requiring VLANs 10 and 20.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR is blind to VLAN 20 traffic and loses segmentation context for untagged traffic, breaking VLAN-aware detection rules and reducing coverage for required VLANs.

recommended_fix.why: Configure broker/SPAN trunk to preserve and forward 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 so NDR receives complete segmented traffic.

findings.root_cause: Microburst of 31.43 Gbps in a 1 ms interval exceeds the NDR's 10 Gbps port capacity by 314% - single tool port is undersized for the aggregated feed with no load balancing or buffering.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR port buffers overflow during bursts causing tool-side drops and incomplete flows, leading to missed detections even though broker shows no drops yet.

recommended_fix.why: Load-balance traffic across multiple NDR ports/instances with flow-aware hashing to absorb 31+ Gbps bursts and prevent tool overload while preserving both directions per flow.
